Full brief: comparator_brief_RI-TEC-036.md

Back to top

Draft policy options

Internal draft These options were signed off at G7 as internal drafts. They are not validated recommendations and have not been prepared for an external audience. Each rests on a validated unresolved gap and on comparator lessons that are agent synthesis, rated conditional. None is proposed because another country adopted it, and none is shown by the evidence to work.

Nationality discrimination in access to employment RI-FMW-001

RI-FMW-001Internal draft Agent synthesis

Option 1: Write equal treatment for EU nationals into the law, as a distinct regime

North Macedonia issue
Nationality discrimination in access to employment (RI-FMW-001)
Comparator it draws on
Croatia, Montenegro
Gap it addresses
the law on access to the labour market does not give EU workers equal treatment with nationals (MKD-EU-2025-001-0097; MKD-EU-2025-003-0033).
Rationale
Croatia (relevance High) and Montenegro (relevance High) each placed EU nationals in a separate regime within their foreigners law, with equal treatment and permit-free work (HRV-EU-2007-001-0015; MNE-GOV-2026-001-0005).
Transferability conditions Agent synthesis
Conditional: the design answers the same mechanism, but neither case shows that it earned the Commission's assessment or changed access for EU workers.
Problem it targets
legal or regulatory gap (MEC-01).
Preconditions
North Macedonia has a separate law on employment of foreigners, so the regime would need to cover that law as well as any residence rules, not one act only; the provisions to be changed would first need to be listed.
Risks
drafting a clause that the Commission does not accept as full alignment, as in Serbia; leaving the reserved private sector posts untouched, since no case covers them.
Responsible actor
the Government, through the ministry responsible for the law on employment of foreigners, now the Ministry of Economy and Labour (MKD-GOV-2025-001-0003, machine translated), with adoption by the Assembly.
Evidence references (5)

“This includes, inter alia, that EU citizens would not need a work permit, and in relation to access to employme nt, may not be discriminated against on the basis of nationality, even if th ey are not yet residing in Croatia.”

HRV-EU-2007-001-0015 · European Commission, Screening report Croatia, Chapter 2 - Freedom of movement for workers, 2007, p. 6 · evidence confidence High

“Odredbe člana 21 st. 7 do 10, člana 68 stav 3 tačka 3, čl. 75, 75a, 75b, 75v i 75g i člana 78 stav 1 tač . 7a i 7v ovog zakona primjenjivaće se od dana pristupanja Crne Gore Evropskoj uniji.”

Machine translation: The provisions of Article 21 paragraphs 7 to 10, Article 68 paragraph 3 point 3, Articles 75, 75a, 75b, 75v and 75g and Article 78 paragraph 1 points 7a and 7v of this Law shall apply from the date of Montenegro's accession to the European Union.

MNE-GOV-2026-001-0005 · Parliament of Montenegro, Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o strancima (Law on amendments to the Law on Foreigners), 2026, p. 40 · evidence confidence Low Evidence limit: machine translated

“The Law on employment of foreigners does not distinguish between EU citizens and other foreigners.”

MKD-EU-2025-001-0097 · European Commission, North Macedonia 2025 Report, SWD(2025) 753 final, 2025, p. 68 · evidence confidence High

“It needs to ensure that by the time of accession, EU citizens can access its labour market without any restrictions.”

MKD-EU-2025-003-0033 · European Commission, Screening report North Macedonia, Cluster 2 - Internal Market, 2025, p. 26 · evidence confidence High

“Во член 5 во ставот (1) зборовите: „министерот надлежен за работите од областа на трудот“ се заменуваат со зборовите: „министерот за економија и труд“. Во ставот (10) зборовите: „министерството надлежно за работите од областа на трудот“ се заменуваат со зборовите: „Министерството за економија и труд“.”

Machine translation: In Article 5 paragraph (1), the words "the minister responsible for labour" are replaced by "the Minister of Economy and Labour". In paragraph (10), the words "the ministry responsible for labour" are replaced by "the Ministry of Economy and Labour".

MKD-GOV-2025-001-0003 · Assembly of North Macedonia (published by the Ministry of Economy and Labour), Закон за изменување на законот за вработување и работа на странци (amending law), Official Gazette 86/25, 2025, p. 1 · evidence confidence Medium Evidence limit: machine translated

RI-FMW-001Internal draft Agent synthesis

Option 2: Settle the commencement design early, rather than assume that deferral to accession is enough

North Macedonia issue
Nationality discrimination in access to employment (RI-FMW-001)
Comparator it draws on
Croatia, Montenegro, Serbia
Gap it addresses
the requirement that EU citizens can access the labour market without restrictions by accession (MKD-EU-2025-003-0033).
Rationale
all three cases. Croatia and Montenegro deferred provisions to accession, and Serbia reported a deferred clause while misalignment findings continued (SRB-EU-2015-001-0002; SRB-EU-2024-001-0004).
Transferability conditions Agent synthesis
Conditional: this is a warning drawn from the tool's reading of three cases, not a tested lesson, and what closed Montenegro's benchmark is not public.
Problem it targets
legal or regulatory gap (MEC-01).
Preconditions
a clear view, through the negotiation process, of which provisions must apply before accession and which may start on accession.
Risks
a law that is aligned on paper but leaves EU workers inside the foreigner regime until accession, which may not satisfy a closing benchmark.
Responsible actor
the Government and its negotiating structures, with the ministry responsible for labour.
Evidence references (3)

“Free access to the Serbian labour market will be provided for EU citizens, as well as their fa mily members, including non-EU citizens. These provisions will enter into force on the date of accession.”

SRB-EU-2015-001-0002 · European Commission, Screening report Serbia, Chapter 2 - Freedom of movement for workers, MD 156/15, 2015, p. 3 · evidence confidence Medium

“Regarding access to the labour market, the legislative framework is partially aligned with the EU acquis as EU citizens are currently covered by rules for third -country nationals.”

SRB-EU-2024-001-0004 · European Commission, Serbia 2024 Report, SWD(2024) 695 final, 2024, p. 70 · evidence confidence High

“It needs to ensure that by the time of accession, EU citizens can access its labour market without any restrictions.”

MKD-EU-2025-003-0033 · European Commission, Screening report North Macedonia, Cluster 2 - Internal Market, 2025, p. 26 · evidence confidence High

RI-FMW-001Internal draft Agent synthesis

Option 3: Do not treat permit simplification or the general non-discrimination rule as the answer

North Macedonia issue
Nationality discrimination in access to employment (RI-FMW-001)
Comparator it draws on
Serbia
Gap it addresses
the Commission's finding that EU citizens are treated as any other foreigner (MKD-EU-2025-001-0097). North Macedonia points to the reference to nationality discrimination in its Law on Labour Relations (MKD-EU-2025-003-0019), but the validated gap judgement finds that this, being the country's own account, does not close the gap.
Rationale
Serbia (relevance Medium) simplified permits for all foreigners and reported a general non-discrimination clause, while the Commission still found that EU citizens were covered by the rules for third-country nationals (SRB-EU-2025-001-0005; SRB-EU-2025-001-0006).
Transferability conditions Agent synthesis
Conditional: the point rests on the Commission's wording, not on a stated lesson, and Serbia's reasons for its slow pace are not in the evidence.
Problem it targets
legal or regulatory gap (MEC-01).
Preconditions
any permit reform would be paired with an explicit provision on EU nationals, as in Option 1.
Risks
reporting progress on procedures while the gap the Commission names remains.
Responsible actor
the ministry responsible for labour, and the Employment Service Agency where permit procedures change.
Evidence references (4)

“Regarding access to the labour market, the legislative framework is partially aligned with the EU acquis as EU citizens are currently covered by rules for third- country nationals.”

Evidence and limits

Validated From the coverage and limits report signed off at G7.

Source coverage

The run met most of its core source requirements for North Macedonia, but with gaps that matter for particular issues. Of 34 requirements, 16 were found, 13 partly found, 3 not found and 2 remain open. The main gaps are the National Programme for the Adoption of the Acquis, for which no version from 2020 onwards could be retrieved; opening or closing benchmarks for Chapter 2, which do not exist because no cluster has been opened; dedicated monitoring of the rights of foreign workers; and the SIGMA and OECD reports, whose publishers block automated download and which were not added by hand. Of 112 registered North Macedonia sources, 99 were available and 13 inaccessible. A large share of the evidence on the country response comes from Macedonian-language government sources and is machine translated, capped at Medium confidence. The comparator pilot used public sources only, with restricted EU documents and blocked sources recorded as gaps (LIM-0028), and extended machine translation to named comparator sources (LIM-0030).

Evidence limit 1,714 of 3,949 in-scope North Macedonia items (43%) are machine translated, and their evidence confidence is capped at Medium. Source quality, evidence confidence and relevance are kept as separate judgements and never combined.

Methodological limitations

The alpha found these limitations, each recorded in the alpha learning log. Extraction missed about one in eight in-scope claims in EU sources, mostly of low importance (LIM-0025, ALN-0017), and the second-pass check may have been applied unevenly between EU and other sources (ALN-0022). The automatic quote check confirms that a quote exists at its location, not that it is cut to the claim (ALN-0013). Only exact file duplicates are detected, so two versions of one screening report were counted twice until an independent check found them (ALN-0023). Parallel agents applied rules differently where the rules were silent, and judged priority inconsistently until a calibration across all issues (ALN-0012, ALN-0026). Agent inputs that were truncated or filtered by issue tag hid relevant evidence in two places (ALN-0025, ALN-0029). In the comparator pilot, first drafts of the cases contained serious errors that routine validation did not catch (ALN-0028), sources stated few lessons, so the case-level lessons are the tool's synthesis (ALN-0031, E15), and passing gates under a standing instruction moved the discovery of a language-limit problem to the end of the pilot (ALN-0030). Since decision E12, no person has read the source documents behind the extraction or the comparator cases; the checks were made by independent agents. Some validated judgement reasons still carry stage 10 wording, such as statuses described as proposals; the values were validated at G6.

Active limits for this run (29)
  • LIM-0008 country · North Macedonia (MKD) only; comparator evidence only for the 2 to 3 issues selected for run 1b
  • LIM-0009 thematic · Run 1 covers all of Chapter 2 (Freedom of movement for workers) plus the technology and AI theme: recommendations materially relating to the areas in taxonomy/themes.csv wherever they occur; incidental references to technology are out of scope; the full analytical chain is followed for every issue originating from an in-scope Chapter 2 item or technology and AI recommendation
  • LIM-0010 thematic · Material outside Chapter 2 and the technology and AI theme is out of scope unless it is needed to follow the analytical chain of an issue already in scope; there is no list of deferred chapters
  • LIM-0011 time · Evidence from 2020-01-01 to the evidence freeze date; earlier material only by logged exception where needed to understand the origin or evolution of an in-scope issue
  • LIM-0012 language · English primary; Macedonian or Albanian only for core relevant sources with no suitable English version; each such source recorded in the register; machine translation flagged and capped at Medium confidence
  • LIM-0013 analytical · No interactive dashboard in run 1 (no country or thematic views); a single static read-only review page (index.html) surfaces validated material and labelled work in progress; outputs remain internal analyst products
  • LIM-0014 evidence · No National Programme for the Adoption of the Acquis (2020 or later) or its implementation reports: the Secretariat for European Affairs site had an expired TLS certificate and no copy was found elsewhere
  • LIM-0015 evidence · No official national material on the European Health Insurance Card or the electronic exchange of social security information (EESSI): the Health Insurance Fund site blocks automated access
  • LIM-0016 accessibility · Documents blocked by publishers for automated download are not retrieved manually in the alpha: SIGMA 2021 and 2024, OECD Competitiveness Outlook 2024 and Labour Migration 2022, UNDP Digital Readiness Assessment, IOM migration profile, two Metamorphosis monitoring reports, the 16th SA Council press statement, State Audit Office originals (ministry copies used)
  • LIM-0017 evidence · Research and civil society coverage of Chapter 2 is thin: one think tank study (MKD-RES-2023-001), evaluation highlights only (MKD-RES-2026-001) and one human rights report (MKD-CSO-2024-001)
  • LIM-0018 language · Almost all national government sources are in Macedonian only (some bilingual with Albanian); evidence on the country response will mostly rely on machine translation capped at Medium confidence
  • LIM-0019 time · Logged exception to the time window: the 2015 Law on Employment and Work of Foreigners (MKD-GOV-2015-001) may be used only where needed to understand the 2021 and 2025 amendments (MKD-GOV-2021-001, MKD-GOV-2025-001)
  • LIM-0021 time · Claims mainly about events before 2020 are kept only as controlled exceptions where needed to explain an in-scope issue; each is flagged out_of_window with the reason and listed for the analyst. Current claims that refer back to earlier events are in scope
  • LIM-0022 thematic · Digital skills are not part of the technology and AI theme; included only where directly linked to an in-scope technology or AI recommendation
  • LIM-0023 thematic · Chapter 2 is read in its EU meaning: rights and access of EU and foreign workers in North Macedonia, labour-market access, equal treatment, EURES, the European Labour Authority, social security coordination, EHIC and anti-corruption measures tied to Chapter 2; emigration, brain drain and diaspora only where directly linked; nationals' access to EU labour markets and general labour-market policy out of scope
  • LIM-0024 time · Extends the exception in LIM-0019 to Art. 5(2) point 1 of the 2015 Law on Employment and Work of Foreigners (MKD-GOV-2015-001), the only provision naming the EU, because a confirmed contradiction on quotas turns on it
  • LIM-0025 evidence · About one in eight in-scope claims may be missed in EU sources, mostly of low importance (37 against 272 items in four sampled sources; the 8 of higher importance added). Long action plans and laws were screened by keyword and section, not read line by line
  • LIM-0026 comparator · Comparator evidence is gathered for three named issues only (RI-FMW-001, RI-TEC-028, RI-TEC-036), as a deliberate expansion approved at G6, with no full country model
  • LIM-0027 time · Logged exception to the time window: comparator documents from 2007 onwards on RI-FMW-001 only, for Croatia, whose reform predates accession in 2013, and Serbia's screening report
  • LIM-0028 accessibility · Comparator evidence uses public sources only. Restricted EU documents are not used, including the EU common position on Montenegro Chapter 2 (AD 26/26), so what closed that benchmark is known only from public statements. Blocked sources, including the SIGMA 2024 reports, are recorded as gaps and not retrieved manually
  • LIM-0029 language · Comparator legal texts in Croatian, Serbian, Montenegrin or Romanian may be used where no English version exists; they are machine-translated and capped at Medium confidence
  • LIM-0030 language · Extends LIM-0029 beyond legal texts to named machine-translated comparator sources: the Moldovan Court of Accounts reports (MDA-GOV-2024-001, MDA-GOV-2024-003), Montenegrin government reports (MNE-GOV-2025-002, MNE-GOV-2025-003, MNE-GOV-2026-003) and the explanatory statement in a Croatian bill (HRV-GOV-2023-002); and to English legal texts available only for payment (the Croatian Aliens Act). All capped at Medium confidence and labelled as such in every output
  • LIM-0031 methodological · No person read the source documents behind the extraction or the comparator cases; extraction, classification and case checks were made by independent agents (E12), with measured error rates reported at each gate
  • LIM-0032 methodological · All analytical judgements were validated by one person, the analyst, as sole decision-maker for the alpha (E13); no second reviewer validated priority, gaps or policy options
  • LIM-0033 methodological · Some validated judgement reasons carry stage 10 wording or rest on mislabelled items, and seven judgements carry rereview_flag (GATE-0012); outputs show the reasons as validated, with a caveat
  • LIM-0034 methodological · Comparator lessons and case-level transferability are agent synthesis, not stated by sources; the cases show what was tried, not what worked, so draft policy options are design options and warnings, not proven routes
  • LIM-0035 methodological · Reform issues are derived from EU requirements, so problems raised only by national or independent sources fit no issue, and issues on themes with thin EU coverage, such as AI, rest on few EU items
  • LIM-0036 time · Refresh (E18): the 2026 Enlargement Package for North Macedonia (country report, factsheet and communication) was not published on 2 November 2026 (due 4 November). Until it is added, every issue's 2026 update is shown as awaiting it; the refresh then adds only it and other official EU material published after the 29 October freeze that materially updates issues already analysed, using the closed run's rule versions
  • LIM-0037 country · The Commission communication "Preparing for a wider Union" and its staff working document on pre-enlargement policy reviews (6 October 2026) are not registered: they review the EU's own policies and budget and do not assess North Macedonia (clear-cut exclusion, country scope; to be surfaced at the refresh G6)
